name: Hero
description: A rigged humanoid: eleven bones, eleven boxes, rigid weights, and two clips — a four-pose walk and a wind-up-strike-recover attack. Built to 1.8 metres so it stands at human height against a one-metre voxel block, and facing +x so it shares the kart's heading convention rather than needing a rotation somewhere to remember. Four sockets, all parented to bones rather than to the body, so a sword in hand_right travels through the swing instead of hovering where the hand started.

sockets.name: hand_right
sockets.description: The striking hand. Parented to forearm.R, so it follows the attack clip through the overhead and down.

sockets.name: head_top
sockets.description: Crown of the head, at the head bone's tail — where a helmet or a crown sits.

sockets.name: back
sockets.description: Between the shoulder blades. -x because the hero faces +x.

animations.name: walk
animations.description: Contact, pass, contact, pass, contact — 25 frames, first and last pose identical so it repeats without snapping. The left foot travels from +0.36m to -0.52m in x, measured on the evaluated rig.

animations.name: attack
animations.description: Guard, wind up, strike, recover. The right hand reaches z=1.64 overhead at the top and lands at x=+0.47 forward, and the spine turns into the blow so the arm is not swinging off a still body.

provenance: The second asset through the Blender bridge and the first rigged one, which is why the schema gained an `animations` array with it: the kart never moves, so nothing until now had a clip that could be silently absent. Dungeon Crawler draws its player as five canvas shapes with a stride phase (generator/figure.ts) — deliberately not an asset, because it must work in any build at any tile size in two projections — and this is what a 3D runtime uses instead once there is one. One LOD tier only, on purpose: at 132 triangles for a whole figure there is nothing to reduce, and inventing lod1-3 to look complete would mean three files claiming a saving they do not make. Rigid weights rather than smooth: the joints are meant to read as joints at this poly count, and it removes a weight-painting step that could quietly produce a different figure on the next build.
